label: Portfolio Hero
title: Portfolio Hero
summary: Use a Portfolio Hero at the top of a holding’s page to show what it is and what it’s worth, with an optional note under the amount.
corePrinciple: The product, its value, then one note.

anatomy.title: A product, an amount, a note
anatomy.description: The product label sits on top, the amount under it, and anything you pass as children under that. Everything is centred.

configuration.title: The logo, its size, and the note
configuration.description: imageSource puts the product’s logo before its label; without it there is no avatar, not an empty circle. Avatar Size sets the logo to 42, 36, or 29 px. children adds what sits under the amount, usually a Badge with the change and a Text with one fact; Slot gap spaces them.

states.title: No states of its own
states.description: The hero doesn’t press, load, or animate, and it has no action: Figma’s Action Slot, an icon button beside the amount, isn’t in the package. What changes is what you pass: a gain or a loss is the Badge in children.

sizing.title: As wide as its amount
sizing.description: The hero has no width of its own: it is as wide as its widest line, usually the amount, plus 8 px on each side, and centres everything. Top to bottom: 8 px of padding, the 29 px label row, 16 px, the amount on a 44 px line, 16 px, then the slot. Figma’s amount sits on a 36 px line, so Figma’s hero is 159 px tall. The amount never wraps or shrinks, so give the hero a host wider than its longest amount.

content.title: The product, the figure, one note
content.description: Write label as the product in a word or two, such as Gold or Mutual Funds. Give value as the formatted figure alone: currency adds the symbol, and INR or ₹ both show ₹. Use children for a caption, such as the change in a Badge and one fact in a Text; a Text there is 12 px, because the hero sets Text Sizes Small. It isn’t a place for a second total.
blocks: INR shows ₹; the grouping stays as you write it.

inContext.title: The top of a holding’s page
inContext.description: The hero opens the Gold page, the holding’s details follow in a list, and the two actions sit at the bottom. Buy ₹1,000 and Sell ₹1,000 change the holding, and the hero shows the new value; the hero has no button of its own.

sources.title: Use the public Portfolio Hero contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (27 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Portfolio Hero has Top Slot, Bottom Slot, and Action Slot switches; the package has a fixed label and amount, children for the slot, and no action. Figma shows the Jio logo by default; the package shows an avatar only with imageSource, and Storybook’s Default story shows a stock photo there instead. The amount sits on a 44 px line, so the hero is taller than Figma’s 159 px (all reported). Screen readers read the amount once, with its currency.
